pages.c04-p01: Explain what a database is, give examples of where databases are used and describe the difference between data and information
pages.c04-p02: Identify tables, records and fields in a database
pages.c04-p03: Choose a suitable data type for each field in a table
pages.c04-p04: Explain what a primary key is and design a table with suitable field names, data types and a primary key
pages.c04-p05: Describe and apply validation checks: range, presence, length, type, format (input mask) and lookup
pages.c04-p06: Describe verification (double entry and visual check) and explain how it differs from validation
pages.c04-p07: Search a database using a query with a single criterion, comparison operators and wildcards
pages.c04-p08: Search a database using multiple criteria with AND and OR, and sort the results
pages.c04-p09: Describe the purpose of forms and reports and what makes a good one
pages.c04-p10: Explain why flat files cause data redundancy and how linking two tables with a foreign key solves this

q.q: What is a database?
o: A list of websites you have visited
A program for drawing graphs and charts
An organised collection of related data
q.why: A database stores related data in an organised way so it can be searched and sorted.

q.q: Which of these is information rather than data?
q.why: It has context, so we know what the data means.

q.q: Which software is a database management system?
q.why: Access is used to create and manage databases.

q.q: Which is an advantage of an electronic database over paper records?
o: It can be searched far more quickly
q.why: Queries search thousands of records in seconds; electronic data can still be wrong or hacked.

q.q: What is a DBMS?
o: Software used to build, search and manage a database
A printed list of records found by a query
A single row of data about one person or thing
A rule that checks entered data is sensible
q.why: Microsoft Access is a database management system.

q.q: What is SIMS an example of in a school?
o: A validation check on pupil data
A flat file with only one table
q.why: The MIS prints registers, reports and timetables.

q.q: How does a supermarket use its database at the till?
o: To show a patient's allergies to a doctor
To pick teams and chase unpaid fees
To update stock levels as items are sold
q.why: The supermarket database also reorders low stock and sends vouchers.

q.q: Why does a hospital database help patients?
o: It stores the hospital's records on paper cards
It lets patients change their own test results
It removes the need for patients to have appointments
Any doctor can quickly see a patient's history and allergies
q.why: Health records in a database can be seen quickly by any doctor.

q.q: Which law must organisations follow because databases hold personal data?
o: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
q.why: Data must be kept secure, accurate and only used for its purpose.

q.q: In a table of pupils, what is a record?
o: All the data about one pupil
q.why: A record is a row.

q.q: The Pupils table has PupilID, FirstName, Surname, TutorGroup, DateOfBirth and Town for 4 pupils. How many fields are there?
q.why: Each column is a field.

q.q: The Pupils table has 6 fields and 4 pupils. How many records are there?
q.why: Each row is one record.

q.q: Which is the best field name for a pupil's home phone number?
q.why: Short, meaningful and no spaces or symbols.

q.q: Which view in Access shows the data in rows and columns like a spreadsheet?
q.why: Design view shows the structure instead.

q.q: What is a field?
o: A screen for entering data one record at a time
The whole collection of tables in a database
One column: one item of data stored about every record
One row: all the data about one person or thing
q.why: Field = the column that goes from top to bottom.

q.q: What does a table in a database store?
o: Every type of data in the school
Data about one type of thing
q.why: e.g. pupils, books or products.

q.q: Why should field names avoid spaces and symbols?
o: Access deletes any field with a space
They can cause problems later in queries
They stop the table from being saved
They make the table print in colour
q.why: Short, clear names like DateOfBirth work best.

q.q: In the Pupils table, Lisnaskea is the Town for record 1002. What is Lisnaskea?
q.why: Each cell holds one item of data.

q.q: Which data type should be used for a pupil's mobile number?
q.why: The leading zero must be kept and no calculations are done on it.

q.q: Which data type is best for the price of a school dinner?
q.why: Currency shows £ and two decimal places.

q.q: A field records whether a library book is on loan. Which data type is best?
q.why: There are only two possible values.

q.q: What does an AutoNumber field do?
o: Rounds every number in the field to a whole number
Adds up all of the numbers in a column for you
Counts how many fields there are in the table
Gives each new record a unique number automatically
q.why: Access fills it in for you: 1, 2, 3...

q.q: What would happen to 02866 322 112 if it were stored in a Number field?
o: It would be stored exactly as it was typed in
It would be turned into a date such as 02/08/66
The leading zero would be removed and spaces not allowed
It would be shown with a £ sign and two decimals
q.why: That is why phone numbers are Short Text.

q.q: Which data type is best for a pupil's medical notes, which may be very long?
q.why: Long Text holds more than 255 characters.

q.q: Which data type is best for StockLevel in a tuck shop table?
q.why: You would add and subtract stock levels.

q.q: Why should DateOfBirth be stored as Date/Time rather than Short Text?
o: So dates sort correctly by year, month and day
So the dates are added up automatically
So the dates cannot be left empty
So the dates are shown with a £ sign
q.why: Text dates would sort alphabetically.

q.q: Which data type is best for a house number such as 12A?
q.why: It contains a letter and is never used in calculations.

q.q: Someone tries to type twelve into a Number field. What does the data type do?
o: It stores it as a Yes/No value
It acts as a type check and rejects it
It accepts it but shows a warning
q.why: The data type stops data of the wrong type.

q.q: Which quick test helps decide whether a field should be Number?
o: Does it contain any digits at all?
Would I ever add, subtract or average this?
Will it appear at the top of the table?
Is it shorter than ten characters?
q.why: If not, it probably should not be a Number field.

q.q: Why is Surname a poor choice of primary key?
o: Two people can have the same surname
It is stored as text, not a number
It changes for most people every year
It is too long to be used as a key
q.why: A primary key must be unique for every record.

q.q: Which would make the best primary key for a table of books?
q.why: Every published edition has its own unique ISBN.

q.q: How is the primary key shown in Access Design view?
o: With a tick box beside it
With a key symbol next to the field
As the last field in the list
q.why: A small key icon appears beside the field name.

q.q: Which of these is not a rule for a primary key?
o: It must be a Currency field
q.why: A primary key can be any suitable data type.

q.q: Two pupils called Conor Kelly are in Year 9. How does a primary key help?
o: It deletes the newer record so only one is left
It sorts both pupils into alphabetical order
It merges the two pupils into one single record
Each has a different PupilID, so they cannot be confused
q.why: PupilID 1027 and 1058 identify them separately.

q.q: A table has no natural unique field. What should you add?
o: A second Surname field for each record
An ID field with the AutoNumber data type
A Long Text field for extra notes
q.why: Access will give each record a unique number.

q.q: Which of these would be a good primary key for a patient table?
q.why: It is unique for each patient.

q.q: What is a table design (data dictionary)?
o: A screen used for entering data one record at a time
A printed report showing all of the records in the table
A drop-down list of allowed values for one of the fields
A plan listing each field's name, data type, description and validation
q.why: It is the information you type into Design view.

q.q: In the library table design, which field is the primary key?
q.why: BookID is an AutoNumber unique for each book.

q.q: In the library table design, OnLoan has a default value of No. What does this mean?
o: The OnLoan field must always be left empty
Only one book can be on loan at any time
Books in the library can never be borrowed
New records start as not on loan unless changed
q.why: A default value is filled in automatically.

q.q: What is validation?
o: Typing data in twice so the two can be compared
A person checking the data against the paper form
An automatic check by the computer that data is sensible
Finding records that match certain criteria
q.why: Validation checks data is sensible and reasonable.

q.q: A field must not be left blank. Which check is needed?
q.why: A presence check makes sure something has been entered.

q.q: Which validation rule would allow only year groups 8 to 14?
q.why: Between is inclusive; >8 And <14 would reject 8 and 14.

q.q: A drop-down list lets the user choose only Red, Blue or Green house. Which check is this?
q.why: The value must match one of a list.

q.q: A pupil's age is entered as 15 instead of 13. Both are within the range check. What does this show?
o: A presence check needs to be added
The field has the wrong data type
Validation cannot check that data is correct
q.why: Validation checks data is sensible, not that it is true.

q.q: In an input mask, what does the character L mean?
q.why: L is a compulsory letter.

q.q: In an input mask, what does the character 0 mean?
o: A letter or digit may be entered
q.why: 9 means a digit may be entered.

q.q: In an input mask, what does > do?
o: Turns the following letters into capitals
Means greater than the last value
Means a letter must be entered
q.why: > converts letters to capitals.

q.q: Which check would an input mask carry out?
q.why: An input mask makes data follow a set pattern.

q.q: Surname has Field Size 30. Which check is this?
q.why: It limits the number of characters.

q.q: What is validation text?
o: The friendly error message the user sees
The pattern used in an input mask
The name of the field being checked
The condition the data must meet
q.why: The validation rule is the condition itself.

q.q: Which value would the rule >=0 And <=50 reject?
q.why: 51 is above the upper limit of 50.

q.q: You type your email address twice when signing up to a website. What is this?
q.why: Typing data twice so the computer can compare is double entry.

q.q: What does verification check?
o: That data is within a sensible range
That data is the correct data type
That a field has not been left empty
That data matches the original source
q.why: Verification checks the data was copied accurately.

q.q: Which mistake would a visual check catch that validation might miss?
o: Letters typed into a Number field
q.why: Mcguire is sensible text, so it passes validation.

q.q: Which statement is true?
o: Validation is automatic and checks data is sensible
Verification is only ever done by the computer
Visual checks never miss any mistakes
Validation proves that the data is correct
q.why: Validation only checks data is reasonable.

q.q: What is a visual check?
o: A drop-down list limits what can be entered
The computer compares two typed versions of the data
A person compares the data on screen with the original document
The computer checks the data is within a range
q.why: A receptionist reading back your details is a visual check.

q.q: What is the main drawback of double entry?
o: It only works on Number fields
It takes twice as long to type
People get tired and miss mistakes
It cannot be used for passwords
q.why: Tiredness is the drawback of a visual check.

q.q: What is the main drawback of a visual check?
o: People get tired or bored and can miss mistakes
It rejects any data outside a set range of values
The data has to be typed in twice by the user
It can only be carried out by the computer
q.why: Double entry's drawback is the extra typing.

q.q: A parent writes the wrong phone number on the paper form. What happens?
o: Validation will always spot that the number is wrong
Validation and verification may both let the wrong number through
Double entry will correct the number automatically
A visual check will always spot the mistake
q.why: Both checks compare with the form, which was wrong.

q.q: An age of 140 is entered. Which would catch it?
q.why: 140 is not sensible, so a range check rejects it.

q.q: Which memory trick helps you remember the difference?
o: Verification is a valid value; validation is verbatim
Both words mean exactly the same thing
Validation is done by people; verification by computer
Verification is verbatim; validation is a valid value
q.why: Verification checks it matches exactly; validation checks it is sensible.

q.q: What is a query?
o: A printable layout of records with totals at the end
A field whose value is unique for every record
A screen used for entering one record at a time
A question that finds the records matching certain criteria
q.why: Access shows only the records that match.

q.q: Which criteria in MathsScore finds scores of 70 or more?
q.why: >= includes 70.

q.q: What does <>"9C" find in the TutorGroup field?
q.why: <> means not equal to.

q.q: Which criteria finds every surname beginning with Mc?
q.why: Mc followed by * (any characters).

q.q: Scores are Aoife 87, Jack 54, Niamh 72, Ryan 91, Cara 45, Ben 68. How many match >=68?
q.why: Aoife, Niamh, Ryan and Ben.

q.q: Using the same scores, how many pupils match >72?
q.why: Only 87 and 91: >72 does not include 72.

q.q: Using the same scores, who matches <=54?
q.why: 54 and 45 are less than or equal to 54.

q.q: In a wildcard search, what does ? stand for?
o: A digit that must be entered
q.why: * stands for any number of characters.

q.q: Which names match Like "B?n"?
q.why: B, then exactly one character, then n.

q.q: Which criteria finds first names that end in a?
q.why: * then a means anything ending in a.

q.q: A pupil types enniskillen in lower case as a criterion. What happens?
o: It finds every town except Enniskillen
It still finds Enniskillen, because criteria are not case sensitive
It finds nothing, because criteria are case sensitive
q.why: Access ignores capitals in criteria.

q.q: In the Access design grid, how are two criteria joined with AND?
o: They are put in separate queries
They are typed on different rows
They are typed on the same Criteria row
They are typed in the Sort row
q.why: Same row = AND; different rows = OR.

q.q: Which usually returns more records?
q.why: OR only needs one condition to be true.

q.q: Pupils: Jack 9B 54, Cara 9B 45, Ryan 9C 91. Who matches TutorGroup "9B" AND MathsScore <50?
q.why: Jack is 9B but scored 54.

q.q: Which list is sorted in descending order?
q.why: Largest to smallest is descending.

q.q: Why does "Enniskillen" And "Lisnaskea" in the Town field find nobody?
o: Town names cannot be used in criteria
No one can live in both towns at once
q.why: AND needs both conditions true for the same record; to find either town you need OR.

q.q: Scores are 87, 54, 72, 91, 45, 68. Which scores match Between 50 And 75?
q.why: Between includes both end values.

q.q: What does ascending order mean for dates?
q.why: Ascending is A to Z, smallest to largest, oldest first.

q.q: A query sorts by two fields. In what order are the sorts applied?
o: By whichever field has more data
q.why: Put the main sort field on the left.

q.q: How else could you find pupils in 9B or 9C in a single criteria box?
q.why: Or in one box does the same as two rows.

q.q: A query finds nothing at all. What do the notes suggest checking first?
o: Whether the table has a primary key
Whether the fields are in Datasheet view
Whether AND was used when OR was meant
q.why: AND narrows the search; OR widens it.

q.q: What is the main purpose of a form?
o: To print a summary of the data held
To make it easy to enter and view records
To link two tables together with a key
To sort the records in a table into order
q.why: Forms are for entering, viewing and editing data.

q.q: A teacher wants a printed list of all pupils who have not paid for a trip. What should be created?
o: A form based on the table
A report based on a query
q.why: A query finds the right pupils; a report presents them.

q.q: Which feature on a form helps to reduce typing errors?
q.why: Choosing from a list stops spelling mistakes.

q.q: Which is a feature of a report rather than a form?
o: Buttons for adding a new record
Records grouped with totals, ready for printing
One record shown at a time for editing
q.why: Reports group and summarise data.

q.q: Can a report be used to change the data in a table?
o: Yes, one record at a time
q.why: Forms can change data; reports cannot.

q.q: Why might a form hide some fields from a receptionist?
o: So the data in those fields needs no validation
So any report made from it prints on one page
So they cannot see or change data they should not
So the form loads much more quickly on screen
q.why: e.g. they can update an address but not see exam results.

q.q: Validation rules are set on the table. Do they still work when data is entered through a form?
o: Yes, they apply in the form too
Only if the form is printed
q.why: The rules belong to the table.

q.q: What should happen to a printed trip report containing medical notes afterwards?
o: It should be recycled with normal paper
It should be kept safe and then shredded
It should be pinned on the noticeboard
It should be given to the pupils
q.why: Data protection law applies to printed personal data.

q.q: What is data redundancy?
o: Data that has been deleted from a table
The same data stored more than once unnecessarily
Data that is stored in a report
Data that fails a validation check
q.why: Repeated data wastes space and causes errors.

q.q: What is a foreign key?
o: A field in one table that is the primary key of another
Any field in a table that contains text
A key used to lock the database with a password
The first field in every table of a database
q.why: It links the two tables together.

q.q: In the linked tables, why is it easier to change 9A's room number?
o: The Pupils table has been deleted
It is stored only once, in the Tutors table
Access changes room numbers on its own
q.why: Change one record and every linked pupil is up to date.

q.q: What is a flat file?
o: A database that has no primary key at all
A report that is printed on a single page
A database stored only on paper cards
A database with all its data in one table
q.why: Flat = one single table.

q.q: In a flat file, 9A's room is B12 in two records and B21 in another. What is this problem called?
q.why: The copies no longer match, so which is correct?

q.q: What is a relational database?
o: Data split into separate linked tables
A database with no primary keys
A database that only holds family data
All data stored in a single table
q.why: Each fact is stored once.

q.q: In the Tutors and Pupils tables, what type of relationship is there?
q.why: One tutor group has many pupils.

q.q: In the Pupils table, TutorGroup is a foreign key. In which table is it the primary key?
q.why: It is the primary key of the Tutors table.

q.q: The last pupil in 9B leaves and is deleted from a flat file. What problem occurs?
o: Mrs Allen is added to every other group
All record of Mrs Allen's tutor group is lost
The table gains a new primary key
q.why: Her details only existed in the pupils' records.

q.q: Where in Access do you link two tables?
o: In the footer of a report
In the Criteria row of a query
q.why: It is on the Database Tools tab.
